issues.legal_issue: An appellate court ordinarily does not disturb concurrent findings of fact that defeat a claim for specific performance when no exceptional basis for interference is shown.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought specific performance of an alleged agreement to sell, asserting that money had been paid toward the price and that possession had been given in part performance.
Both lower courts found that no concluded contract of sale was proved and that the money was advanced as a loan rather than paid toward the price.
The findings rested on the evidence, including oral testimony, and no exceptional circumstance or legal or procedural error justifying interference was established.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent factual findings were not disturbed, and the dismissal of the claim for specific performance was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court ordinarily will not review concurrent findings on pure questions of fact, particularly where they depend on assessing evidence, unless exceptional circumstances justify interference, such as an inference of law from admitted or proved facts or a material violation of law or procedure. The Court referred to Bibhabati v. Ramendra Narayan and described the practice as similar to that of the Judicial Committee.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_specific_performance_d: The proceeding is an appeal in a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.concurrent_findings_on_pure_facts: The lower courts reached the same factual findings on evidence that did not establish the alleged contract.
predicates.exceptional_ground_for_interference: An exceptional circumstance, such as a legal error affecting the finding or a material procedural violation, justifies appellate interference.
predicates.specific_performance_claim_remains_dismi: The claim for specific performance is denied.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a specific-performance suit challenges concurrent findings on pure facts and no exceptional ground for interference exists, the claim for specific performance remains dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff may obtain relief on an alternative factual case that was not pleaded when the defendant expressly admits and relies on that case and granting relief causes no injustice.
material_facts: The plaintiff pleaded that the money was paid toward the price under an alleged contract of sale and sought specific performance, but did not plead a loan as an alternative basis for recovery.
The defendants expressly pleaded that the money was received as a loan, and the courts found that this account was true.
The loan case was expressly raised in the defence, so the defendants had notice of it and no need arose for them to adduce evidence on facts they had admitted.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled to a money decree for the loan even though that alternative case was absent from the plaint and inconsistent with the pleaded claim for specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: A court generally cannot grant relief on a case without a foundation in the pleadings if the opposing party was not called upon or given an opportunity to meet it. But relief may be granted on an alternative case expressly admitted and advanced by the defendant where the defendant cannot be prejudiced and no injustice can result. The Court relied on Babu Raja Mohan Manucha v. Babu Manzoor, in which restitution under section 65 of the Indian Contract Act was allowed despite the absence of an alternative claim in the plaint. The Court also stated that the Civil Procedure Code does not prevent a plaintiff from advancing inconsistent allegations and claiming relief in the alternative.

predicates.civil_suit_with_alternative_money_relief: The proceeding is a civil suit in which the plaintiff seeks relief that can be granted on an alternative factual basis.
predicates.defendant_expressly_admitted_and_relied_: The defendant expressly admitted the alternative facts and put them forward as an answer to the plaintiff's claim.
predicates.no_prejudice_or_injustice_to_defendant: Granting relief on the admitted alternative facts does not surprise or otherwise prejudice the defendant and causes no injustice.
predicates.plaintiff_may_receive_relief_on_alternat: The plaintiff may obtain relief on the alternative factual case.

issues.definition: A plaintiff may receive relief on an alternative factual case when the defendant expressly admits and relies on it and granting relief causes no prejudice or injustice.

issues.legal_issue: Interest is not awarded for a period during which the creditor had possession of property in connection with the debt, but may be awarded after that possession ends when the alleged repayment tender is not established as valid.
material_facts: The money was found to have been advanced as a loan, and the plaintiff had possession of the house until the end of August 1943.
The defendants argued that they had tendered repayment by sending a payment instrument, but the plaintiff denied receiving it and the Court doubted that the alleged act constituted a valid tender.
The defendants had the use of the money after the plaintiff's possession ended.
issues.conclusion: No interest was allowed while the plaintiff remained in possession, but interest at four per cent per annum was awarded from 1 September 1943 until realization; the alleged tender did not defeat that award.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted that interest could not be claimed while the creditor remained in possession of the house. It declined to accept the asserted tender as a basis for denying later interest because receipt was denied and it was doubtful whether the alleged tender was legally valid. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this interest ruling.

predicates.loan_recovery_in_civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal involving recovery of money found to have been advanced as a loan.
predicates.creditor_possessed_property_in_connectio: The creditor held possession of property in connection with the debt.
predicates.possession_ended: The creditor's possession of the property ended while the debt remained unpaid.
predicates.alleged_repayment_tender_not_established: The debtor's alleged repayment tender was denied or was not shown to be legally effective.
predicates.interest_is_awarded_only_for_period_afte: Interest is not awarded for the period of possession but is awarded for the later period when the debt remains unpaid.

issues.definition: When a creditor possessing property in connection with a loan later loses possession and the debtor's alleged repayment tender is not established as valid, interest is awarded only for the period after possession ends.
